To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we measured the noise properties of thin films of superconducting materials with high transition temperatures and that we compared the results for different families of materials.
the noise spectroscopy has been used to study the transport mechanisms in novel superconductors and to set a lower bound to the electronic performances of superconducting devices.

(i) we have measured the noise properties of several high-temperature superconductive materials; (ii) we have found a correlation between the electronic properties of the materials and their noise properties, and (iii) we have shown the importance of noise spectroscopy to evaluate the quality of the materials and to set a limit in their ultimate performances.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of superconducting materials with high critical temperature for possible applications in the field of electronics.
the development of novel electronic devices based on high-Tc superconductors.
the study of the electronic properties of materials with high superconducting critical temperature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, iron-based superconductors are not better materials than cuprates for electronic applications, at least in the normal state.
the noise in the normal state is mainly determined by the material’s resistivity and the Hooge parameter is not strongly dependent on the transition temperature.
the noise properties of the studied materials are not significantly different, and that the Hooge parameter does not show a clear trend with the superconducting transition temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the iron-based superconductors show noise properties similar to those of cuprates, with an Hooge parameter in the range 0.1–0.3.
the Hooge parameter for iron-based superconductors is comparable to that of cuprates.
we have shown that the noise spectroscopy can be a useful technique for the characterization of the electronic properties of the novel superconductive materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the normal conducting state, the noise level is strongly affected by the material’s microstructure, and the Hooge parameter is a useful tool to characterize it.
